sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.4
sources.evidence: March 5, 2026 announcement explicitly releases GPT-5.4 Pro in ChatGPT and the API as gpt-5.4-pro. Separate Pro benchmark columns establish its identity and evaluated reasoning/tool behavior, not parameter counts or shared weights.

sources.title: GPT-5.4 Pro API model documentation
sources.evidence: Exact model record identifies the March 5 dated default snapshot, 1,050,000-token context, 128,000-token output maximum, text/image input, text output, Responses-only access, function calling and medium/default, high and xhigh reasoning. It describes additional compute but neither a shared checkpoint nor prompt caching nor model parameter counts.

sources.title: GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card
sources.evidence: Original release-linked card describes GPT-5.4 Thinking data and RL training. Its complete extracted text has no exact GPT-5.4 Pro identity or shared-model statement; its Thinking specifications and mini appendix cannot establish Pro structure or counts.

sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.5
sources.evidence: April 23 successor announcement includes explicit GPT-5.4 Pro columns for professional, tool-use, academic and abstract-reasoning evaluations. These are benchmark scores, not total/active parameter counts or neural architecture.

sources.title: GeneBench: Assessing AI Agents for Multi-Stage Inference Problems in Genomics and Quantitative Biology
sources.evidence: Later first-party research explicitly evaluates GPT-5.4 Pro and cites its exact API model documentation. Methods report Pro variants under a separate Pro harness using an internal API-like interface. This does not establish shared underlying weights, numerical parameters or topology; 25.6 is a benchmark pass percentage.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 System Card
sources.evidence: Later card explicitly calls GPT-5.5 Pro the same underlying GPT-5.5 model using parallel test-time compute. That relationship is exact to GPT-5.5 and is not evidence of a shared GPT-5.4 Pro checkpoint. No exact GPT-5.4 Pro parameter disclosure appears in the extracted card.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Responses PDF inputs are processed into extracted text and page images for vision-capable models. Combined with exact GPT-5.4 Pro vision and Responses support, this establishes PDF as an API input format, not an additional native modality.

sources.title: OpenAI API changelog
sources.evidence: March 5, 2026 entry explicitly releases GPT-5.4 Pro to Responses, separately from GPT-5.4 Chat Completions and Responses support. Later entries naming only GPT-5.4, such as the March 13 image-encoder fix, are not transferred to Pro.

sources.title: OpenAI API deprecations
sources.evidence: The complete current page was searched for the exact gpt-5.4-pro identifier. No exact Pro shutdown notice was found; GPT-5.4 nano and Cyber notices are distinct. This is not an endpoint-operation test or a statement of current ChatGPT availability.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: The current guide has no explicit GPT-5.4 Pro binding in its supported-model lists. Exact Pro documentation also lacks a prompt-caching feature. Generic family descriptions are insufficient to establish this variant neural architecture.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Section 9.1 reserves service IP and grants limited service use without transferring ownership. Supports a descriptive proprietary classification for this hosted model, not an open-weight license.

sources.title: OpenAI model inventory
sources.evidence: Inventory lists GPT-5.4 Pro as a hosted model, separately from the Apache-licensed gpt-oss open-weight section. Checked exact release/model pages offer no downloadable GPT-5.4 Pro weights.

sources.title: Models.dev GPT-5.4 Pro record
sources.evidence: The original lead was read through its raw file. Generic family and promotional wording were independently checked. Its derived-looking input limit is not substituted for the primary documented total context.

sources.label: GeneBench: Assessing AI Agents for Multi-Stage Inference Problems in Genomics and Quantitative Biology

patch.notes: Released March 5, 2026 in ChatGPT and the Responses API; default API snapshot gpt-5.4-pro-2026-03-05. API context is 1,050,000 tokens with 128,000 maximum output. Reasoning effort supports medium (default), high and xhigh. PDF is an API input format extracted into text and images; image generation is a hosted tool rather than native model output. Total/active parameter counts remain undisclosed and neural architecture unverified in the checked exact-model sources. Additional compute does not establish shared Thinking weights. No exact API shutdown notice was found in the current deprecation page; ChatGPT availability and live API operation were not verified.

summary: Confirmed March 5 release and dated snapshot, 1.05M API context, Pro-specific reasoning controls and function calling. Corrected generation family, proprietary licensing, API PDF format and description. Counts remain undisclosed and exact architecture unverified after original/later cards, exact Pro comparison tables, GeneBench and targeted research checks; no Thinking or successor structure was transferred.
